evidence_loop.label: #645 Codex /hooks attestation import
evidence_loop.summary: runtime:bootstrap resume read the Codex /hooks operator attestation from a top-level doctorReport.codex_hook_review key that runtime:doctor emits on no report, so the import never ran and the non-declinable hooks.codex.attested step could never be satisfied on any hook-bearing bundle, with nothing warning. The loop reads the settings_runs.codex_hook_review currency wrapper doctor actually publishes, judges the claim by the run's own selection instead of doctor's machine-wide verdict, refreshes a stale stored record rather than short-circuiting on its presence, and re-judges the step inside the importing resume.

feature_commits.note: Squash of five review rounds. The PR number is attested rather than derived because the squash subject was passed explicitly with `gh pr merge --subject`, which suppresses the `(#N)` GitHub appends under the repository's PR_TITLE setting; every other release commit in this store carries it.

readings.value: pass; zero hard failures, zero warnings
current; 2026-07-25 baseline 2.1.220 / 0.145.0 unchanged, no compat cycle required
attested and current; settings-20260722T021211Z-364c8f, unaffected because runtime declares no hooks

install_method: Claude host-native `claude plugin marketplace update agentic-plugins` followed by `claude plugin update runtime@agentic-plugins`; the Codex cache was already at 0.86.3 without an explicit command, because its marketplace source is the git remote. No `runtime:settings --execute-plugin-management` executor artifact was produced by this loop, so the installed state rests on the doctor read alone.
narrative:
First live record in this store, authored in the post-release position ADR-0049 requires: the tag, squash, marketplace-sync sha, proof run id and artifact hash all came into existence only after PR #652 merged, release-please cut #653, the catalog sync landed, both hosts were updated, and the proof was re-recorded.

The loop is one deliverable, but it took five cross-host review rounds and the first three each found a real defect. The first cut gated the import on doctor's `current` verdict; that is wrong, because doctor judges the whole machine while bootstrap judges a selection, so the gate stranded a step the reducer calls satisfiable. Fixing the read path also made two pre-existing defects reachable for the first time: a stored record could never be refreshed once written, and the resume that imported the claim left its own step pending — meaning the path fix alone did not deliver the issue's stated expectation. A later round then introduced and removed a regression of its own, in which re-judging from the pre-answer snapshot discarded operator declines recorded earlier in the same resume.

Two paths that can also leave `hooks.codex.attested` permanently unsatisfiable were found and deliberately not fixed here: two Codex-version parsers disagree on SemVer build metadata, and an obsolete disabled hook row for a still-selected plugin lets settings attest while bootstrap stales. They share one root — bootstrap's probe serialization is a less faithful reader of the machine than settings' and doctor's — and are recorded together in plugins/runtime/docs/follow-ups.md. Neither affects this machine or the reporter's (both Codex 0.145.0, no build metadata).
